macro.regime: Tentative risk rebound, hard-asset rotation intact
macro.narrative: Friday 21 Aug delivered a broad-based equity rebound (S&P +0.43% to 7,674.37, Dow +0.98%, Russell +0.85%) and a cooling VIX (-5.5% to 15.13), as Treasury Secretary Bessent's confirmation that the doubled long-bond buyback could exceed the $4bn/operation floor extended the real-yield relief trade that began Wednesday. Gold and silver notched a third straight day of gains (GLD +1.95%, SLV +1.72%, gold futures +3.22% to $4,661.60) on continued dollar weakness (DXY near an 11-week low) and building hedge demand ahead of the 27-29 Aug Jackson Hole Symposium, where new Fed Chair Warsh delivers his untested first keynote (28 Aug; a BofA survey shows 69% expect a neutral tone, leaving room for a hawkish surprise). Rare-earth names staged a sharp, policy-driven reversal of Thursday's AI-fear-driven selloff — MP +9.10%, UUUU +8.92% — on G7 leaders' agreement to cut rare-earth reliance on non-bloc (China) suppliers, a Pentagon-backed $500M Phoenix Tailings loan, and the DoE's selection of seven critical-mineral processing/battery projects, making Materials the S&P's strongest sector (+2.09%). Xiaomi's outsized +4.54% move (Thu HK close, index data still lagging) reflects continued digestion of its 18 Aug Q2 results (EV deliveries +28.2% YoY, SkyNomad SUV pre-orders >100k) rather than fresh news. Trump's Friday 7pm ET remarks were confirmed to be a South Carolina Senate campaign rally (endorsing Darline Graham ahead of the 25 Aug runoff), not a market-moving policy event, while the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial shipping with continued Iranian tanker seizures — a structural oil-risk premium that held Brent/WTI roughly flat Friday after the week's sharp climb.
